conviction_note: Two counter-signals roughly cancel. The mortgage proxies are negative: a close correspondent peer's July-August production fell about 28% a month, and mortgage rates hit 7.4-7.5% in October, against a guide of mortgage revenue 'in line with Q2'. Against that, NII rises with rates, credit resolutions are already guided, the buyback runs at 1.16x TBV, and puts are bid into a modest, rising short. So impact_sum is about 0 and p_up 48 on an abs move of 5.0, which gives -0.2. The abs move sits between the 7.98% implied move and the 3.24% median realised move, because hunters have run too small and Zions reports the same night.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $2.49 and revenue about $994m (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/WAL), and $2.46 / $992.5m (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WAL/earnings-forecasts). The two sources roughly agree. The company gives no quarterly EPS guide. Its FY2026 guide from the Q2 deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001212545/000162828026049001/walq22026earningspresent.htm): NII +12-14% (assumes a 25bp September hike), non-interest income +13-17% (cut from 20-25%), loans +$5bn, deposits +$6bn, NIE ex deposit costs $1.60-1.65bn, deposit costs $650-700m, NCO 25-35bp, CET1 about 11%. Q3 commentary: mortgage banking revenue in line with Q2; loans +$1.2-1.3bn; deposit costs lower; $150m buyback in H2.
positioning_check: Short interest is 6.22m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 5.36m on 2026-08-14 and 5.97m on 2026-09-15. That is about 5.7% of shares outstanding and 4.73 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/wal/shortinterest, read 2026-10-19). Short interest is rising but not crowded. The baseline 25-delta skew is +4.79 vol points (downside paid), put/call open interest is 2.02, and the event-implied move of 7.98% is well above the 3.24% median and 5.14% maximum of the last 7 realised reactions. The stock is -6.47% over 20 days, -23.4% from its 52-week high and +10.3% off its 52-week low. Spot is $73.57 against Q2 TBV of $63.24 (1.16x).

findings.finding: PennyMac is WAL/AmeriHome's closest correspondent-aggregator peer. Its preliminary funding was $16.6bn for July-August 2026 against $34.9bn for all of Q2, about 28% lower a month, as mortgage rates rose to about 7.0-7.3% in September. WAL guided Q3 mortgage banking revenue 'in line with Q2' (Q2: $53.4m gain on sale plus $31.3m net servicing, about 8.5% of revenue). AmeriHome Q2 production was $16.2bn with a 29bp gain-on-sale margin. A comparable volume drop would put Q3 mortgage revenue roughly $10-20m (about $0.07-0.14 EPS) below the guide, unless margins widen or higher rates lift MSR and servicing value.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21): the non-interest income guide was cut from 20-25% to 13-17% on mortgage headwinds while the NII guide was raised, and the stock rose 3.61% (baseline). The market looked through a fee cut when NII held. Q1 2026 gain on sale was $72.7m and fell to $53.4m in Q2, inside that +3.61% print.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS sits flat-to-up on Q2 ($2.46-2.49 against $2.36), which implies no fee shortfall. If a 20%+ correspondent volume drop were in the bar, the revenue estimate would sit below Q2's $995.7m rather than at $992-994m with NII growing. A specialist mortgage-trade article, not bank-analyst coverage, carried it.
findings.independence: Proxy, not WAL's own number. Freddie Mac PMMS shows the 30-year at 6.71% on 2026-09-03 and 7.03% on 2026-09-24 (https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mortgage-rates-average-671). This shares the rate driver with the Q4-guide finding below, but the quarter and document are different.

findings.finding: Mortgage rates moved higher again in October: MBA's 30-year conforming reached 7.50% for the week ending 2026-10-09 (+53bp in four weeks, highest since November 2023), refinance applications were 56% below a year earlier and purchase applications 16% below. Freddie Mac reads 7.40% on 2026-10-15. WAL's guide that mortgage banking holds at Q2 levels for Q3 AND Q4 was set at about 6.7%. The Q4 outlook for AmeriHome and mortgage-warehouse balances will likely be cut, and with it a third cut to the non-interest income range. Lower warehouse deposits are about 100% beta, though, so lower ECR deposit costs partly offset.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The fee guide cut in Q2 2026 came with a +3.61% reaction because NII was raised. Q2 2025 (-3.98%) and Q4 2024 (-5.14%) are the larger down reactions in the baseline, with no line attribution available.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is -6.5% over 20 days, with puts bid, as rates rose. Sell-side numbers aggregated on 2026-10-19 still show Q3 revenue near Q2 levels. If a Q4 fee cut were fully in, the 20-day decline would likely show up as estimate cuts on the aggregators, and none were found.
findings.independence: Shares the rate driver with the PennyMac finding (different quarter, different document). The MBA 2027 originations markdown points the same way (https://www.mpamag.com/us/mortgage-industry/market-updates/2027-mortgage-originations-to-fall-5-to-199-trillion-mba-forecasts/593085).

findings.finding: The Fed raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and the dot plot implies one more 2026 hike. WAL's FY NII guide (+12-14%) assumed only the September hike, and its own sensitivity is +3.2% NII per +100bp ramp. A further hike is slight upside to NII guidance, partly offset by ECR deposit costs repricing in Q4 (management flagged that).
findings.why_not_priced: The hike itself is in the guide and priced. Only an extra hike beyond the guide's assumption would be new to the NII range, and a weak tape (-6.5% over 20 days) suggests the market is reading higher rates as negative for this bank (fees, AOCI) rather than positive for NII.
findings.independence: WAL's Q2 deck sensitivity table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001212545/000162828026049001/walq22026earningspresent.htm). Shares that deck with the bar.

findings.finding: The 10-year Treasury rose 85bp in Q3 2026, the biggest quarterly rise since 2016 (WSJ/Dow Jones data). WAL holds a $20.6bn securities portfolio, of which the AFS share sits in AOCI. That implies an AOCI hit that may leave Q3 TBV per share (Q2: $63.24) flat to down despite about $2 a share of retained earnings, and could slow TCE/TA growth and the buyback pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 TBV rose $2.10 with a 'modest improvement in AOCI', and the stock rose 3.61%. No prior print where TBV fell on AOCI is identified in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Yields are public and the market can estimate this; the AFS/HTM split and duration are not in the Q2 deck, so the exact TBV print is not knowable. Probably mostly priced by the 20-day decline.
findings.independence: Macro-to-company inference, not confirmed by WAL; AFS size not found in the Q2 deck. None.

findings.finding: Peer read-through from regionals that reported 2026-10-15/16 is modestly positive: M&T EPS $5.04 ($5.08 adjusted) against $4.98 consensus, revenue $2.55bn against $2.53bn; Regions $0.71 against $0.66 consensus with interest-bearing deposit costs of 1.70%; Independent Bank NIM up 4bp. No sector credit scare has surfaced in this cycle.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: October 2025: a sector credit scare (Zions/WAL shared fraud borrower) moved WAL about -10% in a day, so WAL trades with regional credit news.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced since the peer prints are already out, yet WAL still trades near its 52-week low end (+10% off the low) with puts bid. That suggests the market has not given WAL credit for a clean sector quarter, likely because WAL's mortgage-linked fee mix differs from the peers'.

findings.finding: Zions Bancorporation also reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-10-19, inside the same window. In October 2025 the two banks fell 13% and about 11% together on a shared fraud borrower, so Zions' credit print is a correlated shock to WAL's reaction in either direction. Its sign is unknown before both releases.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-16: Zions -13%, WAL about -10% on the shared-borrower disclosure; KRE -6.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Not directional. It widens the outcome distribution, which the 7.98% implied move against a 3.24% realised median may already reflect.
findings.independence: Bloomberg Law on the October 2025 episode (https://news.bloomberglaw.com/banking-law/zions-western-alliance-disclose-bad-loans-tied-to-alleged-fraud).

findings.finding: Credit is tracking to plan. On the Q2 call management named six problem credits for resolution: two closed in Q2, a third within 1-2 weeks, a fourth targeted for end-Q3 and two in Q4. They expect total NPLs to fall in H2 (nonaccruals were 0.92% of HFI loans at Q2), special mention fell $87M to $316M, and they said charge-offs peaked in Q1/Q2. Core NCO guide is 25-35bp, with H2 tracking slightly above the midpoint, and the ACL is expected to rise about 2bp a quarter. No 8-K since 2026-07-30 (EDGAR) signals any credit event.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 had a 1.45% headline NCO (fraud-related) and the stock still rose 0.69% on 2026-04-21. Q2 2026 nonaccruals rose $70m and the stock still rose 3.61%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside guidance, so mostly priced. A visible NPL decline is the one credit outcome the put skew (+4.8) does not price.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions show only dividend, Form 4 RSU-cash-settlement and 13G filings since July (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001212545.json). Absence of a filing is weak evidence.

findings.finding: The planned $150m H2 2026 buyback is now executing at about $73-79 a share, roughly 1.16-1.25x Q2 TBV. That is about 1.7% of the roughly $8.1bn market cap and accretive to TBV; management may also deploy about 81bp of CET1 freed by Basel III changes into 2027 buybacks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a larger buyback emphasis came with the +3.61% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Already guided. Only an upsized pace, or the 2027 CET1 release confirmed, would be new.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 transcript with the credit finding. Q2 release shows $120.4m repurchased cumulative under the $300m program (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001212545/000162828026049001/pressrelease-6302026.htm).

findings.finding: Deposit remix is running: about $1bn of higher-cost deposits had already moved off by late July, with about $750m more expected by quarter-end. Management guided Q3 deposit costs lower and total deposits up about $1bn in Q3. Lower mortgage-warehouse balances (100% beta) would cut deposit costs further, partly offsetting the fee drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 deposits fell $849m QoQ on the deliberate remix and the stock rose 3.61%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside guidance, mostly priced. The offset to the mortgage-fee finding is what the consensus may underweight.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the credit and buyback findings.

findings.finding: Positioning leans against a negative surprise. Short interest has risen four settlements running to 6.22m shares (about 5.7% of shares, 4.73 days to cover), puts carry a +4.79 vol-point skew with put/call open interest at 2.02, and the stock is -6.5% over 20 days to 1.16x TBV. A merely in-line print with stable NII guidance can see shorts and put holders cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of the last 7 reactions were up, including +3.61% into a fee-guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew says the market expects downside. This finding only says the setup is asymmetric if that downside fails to show, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline options block (skew, put/call OI, run-up).

baseline_tension: The mortgage-rate findings agree with the +4.8 put skew and the -6.5% 20-day slide, so they are likely partly priced. The NII, credit, buyback and positioning items cut against the skew. Net, the evidence is balanced, and p_up sits at 48 rather than below 45.
lessons_applied: Rules 5 and 9: the two mortgage findings are peer/macro proxies on a line worth about 8.5% of revenue, net of NII growth, so each shrinks: PennyMac -0.8 to -0.6, Q4 rate guide -0.8 to -0.5.
Rule 1: the Q2 2026 fee-guide cut came with +3.61%, so this name has looked through fee cuts when NII held; this is reflected in the mortgage sizes, not cut again.
Rule 7: the positioning finding goes against a +4.8 put skew, so +0.5 shrinks to +0.3.
Rule 6: the credit finding lands inside the guided NCO range, so +0.3 goes to +0.2. The bar is sourced to two roughly agreeing estimate sources, so no cap.
Rule 5: the peer read-through is a proxy, so +0.3 goes to +0.2.
